Subject: UK IDTA / TIA: potential onshore exception and subprocessor list

Kimberly / Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. We are moving Redwood forward with a pilot for UK clinical routing but the legal team has flagged two items we need resolved before procurement: an explicit UK IDTA (or UK Addendum) position and the accompanying TIA/DTIA evidence for subprocessors that will touch patient data.

Specific asks from Greenline:
- Can Redwood provide a redline of the UK Addendum you expect to sign (we need the version that will be attached to our DPA).
- Full subprocessor roster for the services that will process UK data and the technical safeguards (KV cache retention, onshore cache fallback, HSM usage).
- A TIA/DTIA-style package (high-level architecture diagram + controls mapping) for the route you propose (hosted API with UK-edge cache fallback).
- Whether you can accept an interim "onshore-localization exception" for our pilot that restricts persistent logs to UK region while allowing ephemeral offsite inference for short bursts (we need a timeline for when full UK-residency is available).

Legal copied here (legal+gdpr). Please advise next steps — if helpful we can set a 30-min call to walk architecture.

Regards,
Alice Summers
Head of Privacy Operations
Greenline Health

Proposed next steps (quick):
1) Ill attach our current UK Addendum redline for review (legal to legal).
2) Jonas will share a transfer-impact matrix that maps subprocessors -> controls -> evidence (encryption in transit/at rest, HSM, KV cache retention policy).

Can you do a 30-min sync Wednesday 19 May 10:00 UK / 05:00 PDT? If that slot doesn't work tell us a couple of alternatives.

Alice / team —

Attached is a first-pass transfer-impact matrix and a one-page architecture snapshot. High-level notes:
- Subprocessors in-scope for the pilot: inference pool (eu-west-1), observability pipeline (vendor: LogStream), key management (KMS provider), and a CDN for customer-facing assets.
- Controls: TTL for in-memory KV cache is 30s by default; persistent request logs are routed to UK S3 buckets when tenant is marked UK-resident. For the pilot we can expand the persistent log routing to ensure log objects are written to the UK bucket within the same request flow (adds ~20ms median latency).
- HSM usage: customer-managed keys via our KMS integration supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers we offer Redwood-managed keys (we can provide attestations).

If Greenline needs a DTIA we can assemble the following artifacts for each subprocessor: SOC2 Type II summary, encryption algorithm and key custody note, network flow diagram, and a screenshot of retention policy in our console. I attached the matrix and the draft RBAC/edge-routing diagram.

Jonas Weber
Senior Privacy Engineer

- The onshore localization exception wording needs to be explicit about which artifacts are considered "persistent logs" vs "ephemeral inference state". Were comfortable with ephemeral offsite inference if pseudonymization is applied at the request layer and no persistent PII leaves UK buckets.
- Please confirm whether Redwood will accept DocuSign with our redline (we will send a counterproposal to the UK Addendum) and whether the 90-day timebox for the pilot is acceptable.
- For the TIA, can you confirm which substantiating documents you can deliver within 10 business days (we need them for our procurement signoff): SOC 2 summary, KMS attestation, and the network flow diagram with region tags.

If you confirm the timeline well route the redline internally and target signing the pilot contract by end of next week.

Best,
Alice

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: UK IDTA / TIA: potential onshore exception and subprocessor list

Alice —

We reviewed the redline and the matrix. We can accept the proposed 90-day, timeboxed localization exception for a pilot provided Greenline signs a limited-scope amendment to the DPA documenting:
- Exact definitions: "persistent logs" = any records persisted to object storage or long-term analytics buckets; "ephemeral inference state" = KV cache and in-memory model state with TTL < 120s.
- Compensating controls required during the exception: pseudonymization at request edge, per-tenant encryption with customer-managed KMS where requested, and monthly evidence snapshot from Redwood (SOC2 executive summary + KMS attestation).
- Transition plan: Redwood will provide a target schedule (no longer than 90 days) for enabling full UK residency for persistent backups or an agreed export escrow process.

We can deliver the SOC2 summary, KMS attestation, and a region-tagged network flow diagram within 7 business days after the amendment is agreed. We will also push a DocuSign envelope with our redline to the UK Addendum today (link included below).

If that works for Greenline, Kimberly / Jonas — please confirm we should proceed to DocuSign and Ill track execution and evidence delivery tasks.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
